title: Conservation of momentum
statement: state the principle of conservation of momentum

title: Solving collision problems with momentum
statement: apply the principle of conservation of momentum to solve simple problems, including elastic and inelastic interactions between objects in both one and two dimensions (knowledge of the concept of coefficient of restitution is not required)

title: Elastic collisions and kinetic energy
statement: recall that, for an elastic collision, total kinetic energy is conserved and the relative speed of approach is equal to the relative speed of separation

title: Momentum conserved, kinetic energy may change
statement: understand that, while momentum of a system is always conserved in interactions between objects, some change in kinetic energy may take place

title: Centre of gravity
statement: understand that the weight of an object may be taken as acting at a single point known as its centre of gravity

title: Moment of a force
statement: define and apply the moment of a force

title: Couples as pure rotation forces
statement: understand that a couple is a pair of forces that acts to produce rotation only

title: Torque of a couple
statement: define and apply the torque of a couple

title: Principle of moments
statement: state and apply the principle of moments

title: Equilibrium of forces and torques
statement: understand that, when there is no resultant force and no resultant torque, a system is in equilibrium

title: Vector triangle for forces in equilibrium
statement: use a vector triangle to represent coplanar forces in equilibrium

title: Defining density
statement: define and use density

title: Defining pressure
statement: define and use pressure

title: Deriving hydrostatic pressure
statement: derive, from the definitions of pressure and density, the equation for hydrostatic pressure $\Delta p = \rho g \Delta h$

title: Using hydrostatic pressure equation
statement: use the equation $\Delta p = \rho g \Delta h$

title: Upthrust from pressure difference
statement: understand that the upthrust acting on an object in a fluid is due to a difference in hydrostatic pressure

title: Calculating upthrust, Archimedes' principle
statement: calculate the upthrust acting on an object in a fluid using the equation $F = \rho g V$ (Archimedes' principle)

title: Work done by a force
statement: understand the concept of work, and recall and use work done = force × displacement in the direction of the force

title: Conservation of energy
statement: recall and apply the principle of conservation of energy

title: Efficiency as a ratio of energies
statement: recall and understand that the efficiency of a system is the ratio of useful energy output from the system to the total energy input

title: Solving efficiency problems
statement: use the concept of efficiency to solve problems

title: Defining power
statement: define power as work done per unit time

title: Solving power problems, P = W/t
statement: solve problems using $P = W/t$

title: Deriving and using P = Fv
statement: derive $P = Fv$ and use it to solve problems

title: Deriving gravitational potential energy change
statement: derive, using $W = Fs$, the formula $\Delta E_P = mg\Delta h$ for gravitational potential energy changes in a uniform gravitational field

title: Using gravitational potential energy change
statement: recall and use the formula $\Delta E_P = mg\Delta h$ for gravitational potential energy changes in a uniform gravitational field

title: Deriving kinetic energy formula
statement: derive, using the equations of motion, the formula for kinetic energy $E_K = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$

title: Using the kinetic energy formula
statement: recall and use $E_K = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$

title: Deformation by tensile or compressive forces
statement: understand that deformation is caused by tensile or compressive forces (forces and deformations will be assumed to be in one dimension only)

title: Load, extension and limit of proportionality
statement: understand and use the terms load, extension, compression and limit of proportionality
